item.research_question: How can single-phase refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) be designed to achieve ultrahigh yield strength at 1600°C, and what is the underlying deformation mechanism responsible for the observed plateau strength?
item.material_system: Hf0.5MoNbTaW and HfMoNbTaW refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs)
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting followed by homogenization treatment at 2100°C for 2 hours with subsequent air cooling in an ultrahigh-temperature furnace under Ar flow
item.test_conditions: Compression testing at a strain rate of 10⁻³ 1/s from ambient temperature to 1600°C; samples were 3.6 mm in diameter and 6 mm in height for 1600°C tests
key_findings: HfMoNbTaW alloy after homogenization exhibits a yield strength of 571 MPa at 1600°C, which is higher than MoNbTaVW (477 MPa).
A plateau of strength occurs from 800°C to 1200°C for HfMoNbTaW, with a value of approximately 950 MPa.
Homogenization at 2100°C for 2 h results in a homogeneous body-centered cubic (bcc) phase with no precipitation.
The theoretical yield strength (σycal) for HfMoNbTaW increases by 30.8% from 2393 MPa to 3131 MPa upon equiatomic addition of Hf into MoNbTaW.
The shear modulus of HfMoNbTaW was measured to be 73 ± 1 GPa via nanoindentation.
Extrapolation of high-temperature strength data suggests a room temperature strength of 4536 MPa, consistent with edge dislocation control calculations (4206 MPa).
Adding Hf to MoNbTaW increases yield strength by 47.5% compared to MoNbTaW (1561 MPa vs 1058 MPa).
item.mechanism: The authors propose that the plateau strength and ultrahigh elevated-temperature strength result from a transition in the deformation mode from screw dislocations to edge dislocations. Below the critical temperature (Tc), strength decreases due to thermal activation of screw dislocations. Above Tc, edge dislocations become dominant in general yielding, leading to a plateau in strength and high strength at elevated temperatures.
item.limitations: The text notes that the theoretical yield strength calculated using the average shear modulus (Gmix) is generally larger than the experimental value, and that the assumption of mixed dislocation control (α=9) was an overestimate compared to screw dislocation control (α=2) at low temperatures.
item.future_work: The authors state that a similar alloy design strategy could be applied to develop more RHEAs with an ultrahigh strength level.
quotes: HfMoNbTaW alloy exhibits a yield strength of 571 MPa at 1600°C, much higher than that of MoNbTaVW (477 MPa).
This strengthening mechanism is explained with the change of deformation mode from screw to edge dislocations, which contributes an edge-dislocation-induced strength.
The edge dislocation becomes dominant in general yielding and results in high strength at high temperatures above Tc.
